**3. Layout:**
The diagram illustrates the architecture and threat model of a SaaS LLM application. The left side and bottom right feature cloud-shaped regions representing untrusted internet mediums. The central and upper sections represent the inference pipeline, containing Ingress, Application Services, LLM Production Services (with Agents and the LLM Model), Vector DB, RAG Private Data Stores, and Server-side functions. The lower-left and bottom-center areas contain the data and training workflows, showing an ML Engineer, Data Scientist, Fine-tuning Data, Training Data, and External Data Sources. OWASP Top 10 vulnerability tags (LLM01 through LLM10) alongside associated CWE, API, and AML identifiers are overlaid across their corresponding components and trust boundaries.

**4. Flow:**
Prompts flow from the client through Ingress into Application Services and LLM Production Services, which interact with Vector DB and private RAG data stores via semantic queries and vector matching, and with server-side functions via execution and storage calls. Concurrently, data flows from External Data Sources, overseen by the ML Engineer and Data Scientist, through dataset processing into Training and Fine-tuning Data to supply the LLM Model.
